## ARGUMENT

### I. A shotgun pleading that fails to give defendants adequate notice of the claims against them warrants dismissal.

Rule 8(a)(2) requires "a short and plain statement of the claim showing that the pleader is entitled to relief," and Rule 10(b) requires that each claim founded on a separate transaction or occurrence be stated in a separate count. Together, these rules ensure that a defendant can discern what he is being sued for and frame a response. This Court has long condemned complaints that defeat that purpose. *See Cramer v. Florida*, 117 F.3d 1258, 1263 (11th Cir. 1997); *Anderson v. Dist. Bd. of Trs. of Cent. Fla. Cmty. Coll.*, 77 F.3d 364, 366–67 (11th Cir. 1996).

**A. The governing standard.** In *Weiland v. Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office*, this Court identified four rough categories of shotgun pleadings. These are complaints that (1) incorporate every preceding paragraph into each successive count; (2) are replete with conclusory, vague, and immaterial facts not obviously connected to any cause of action; (3) fail to separate each cause of action into a distinct count; or (4) assert multiple claims against multiple defendants without specifying which defendant is responsible for which act. 792 F.3d 1313, 1321–23 (11th Cir. 2015). The "unifying characteristic" of all of them is that they "fail to one degree or another, and in one way or another, to give the defendants adequate notice of the claims against them and the grounds upon which each claim rests." *Id.* at 1323; *accord Strategic Income Fund, L.L.C. v. Spear, Leeds & Kellogg Corp.*, 305 F.3d 1293, 1295 & n.9 (11th Cir. 2002) (criticizing counts that incorporate all prior allegations).

**B. The harm is not merely formal.** This Court has repeatedly explained that shotgun pleadings burden both litigants and the judiciary. A defendant faced with such a pleading cannot readily tell which allegations support which claim, and the court cannot readily separate meritorious claims from meritless ones. *See Magluta v. Samples*, 256 F.3d 1282, 1284 (11th Cir. 2001) (per curiam) (describing the burden imposed by a lengthy, disorganized complaint). Such pleadings also expand discovery and consume judicial resources. *Jackson v. Bank of Am., N.A.*, 898 F.3d 1348, 1356–58 (11th Cir. 2018). Dismissal on this ground is therefore not a technicality. It is a proper exercise of the district court's authority to manage its docket and to require compliance with Rules 8 and 10. *Id.* at 1357–58; *Paylor v. Hartford Fire Ins. Co.*, 748 F.3d 1117, 1125–26 (11th Cir. 2014).

**C. Dismissal is appropriate where, as here, a plaintiff has been given notice and an opportunity to cure.** Where a complaint is a shotgun pleading, the district court should ordinarily identify the deficiencies and give the plaintiff one chance to replead. *Vibe Micro, Inc. v. Shabanets*, 878 F.3d 1291, 1295–96 (11th Cir. 2018). When the plaintiff fails to cure those deficiencies, dismissal is within the court's discretion. *See id.*; *Barmapov v. Amuial*, 986 F.3d 1321, 1324–25 (11th Cir. 2021) (affirming dismissal of a shotgun pleading and noting that the plaintiff's failure to correct it after being given the opportunity justified dismissal).

**D. Plaintiff's complaint falls squarely within *Weiland*.** [Tailor to record.] The operative complaint incorporates all preceding allegations into each count, so that later counts rest on the legal conclusions of earlier ones. It combines distinct causes of action in single counts. And it directs its allegations at "Defendants" collectively, without identifying which defendant is alleged to have committed which act. Under *Weiland*, each of these defects independently marks the complaint as a shotgun pleading, and together they left Defendant unable to determine what conduct it was alleged to have committed or which claims it must answer. 792 F.3d at 1321–23. The district court gave Plaintiff notice of these deficiencies and an opportunity to cure them, and Plaintiff failed to do so. Dismissal was a sound exercise of discretion and should be affirmed. *Vibe Micro*, 878 F.3d at 1295–96; *Barmapov*, 986 F.3d at 1324–25.
